# Rustix agent instructions

These instructions apply to every coding agent working in this repository. Read this file before changing code. For the architecture and detailed subsystem contracts, use the linked documents under `docs/`; this file summarizes the rules agents must preserve.

## Project mission

Rustix is an experimental 64-bit, Unix-like operating system with its own Rust kernel. Limine is the external boot protocol/loader only. Do not describe Limine, a host shell, or a userspace project as the Rustix kernel.

The kernel is `no_std` and targets `x86_64-unknown-none`. Rust is the implementation language for kernel and OS components. The repository currently uses a Python standard-library script only to assemble and smoke-test the boot image; it does not replace kernel or OS functionality.

Unix-like behavior is a long-term design goal, not a claim of POSIX compatibility. Make unsupported behavior explicit rather than approximating it silently.

## Current project status — read before planning

The source contains:

- A Limine-based x86_64 kernel entry, linker layout, serial diagnostics, and boot-memory reporting.
- A separate allocation-free `no_std` `crabshell` parser crate and a kernel-mode COM1 shell frontend.
- A volatile, fixed-capacity RAM filesystem used by the shell.
- A validated, fixed-capacity boot memory-map snapshot and baseline CPUID/address-width reporting.
- A fixed-capacity physical frame allocator retained in `BootInfo`; Crabshell's `meminfo` command reports counts. No kernel service currently allocates frames for mappings or other services.
- Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup and fatal exception handlers for vectors 0–31. Double faults use an IST stack and page faults report CR2. Maskable IRQs remain disabled; exception recovery and fault-injection tests are not implemented.

Important incomplete work:

- Milestone 0's local exit criteria were met on 2026-10-16: `just verify` passed from both the working tree and a clean detached worktree in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04. The detached worktree had an empty `target` directory, so the run exercised fresh Limine download/host-tool compilation, formatting, 19 host tests, target check, optimized build, image creation, and the 20-second QEMU prompt smoke test. Hosted CI has not been observed.
- A separate interactive `just run` session exercised directory navigation and create/write/append/read/copy/move/list/remove operations; `cp` replaced an existing destination, `rmdir` rejected a nonempty directory and succeeded after its child was removed, and unsupported `memtest` was rejected as expected. Boot snapshot tests and QEMU boot-metadata reporting were exercised. Structural checks still cannot prove that a Limine-provided non-null pointer is mapped or readable; that remains a loader trust boundary.
- Milestone 0 is closed for local acceptance; hosted CI remains pending. Milestone 1's validation criteria are met for the current Limine path, subject to the documented pointer-readability trust boundary. Milestone 2 is **in progress**, not complete. The frame allocator now specifies token ownership and preserves the token on failed deallocation; unique allocator-instance use is still caller-enforced. Rustix still inherits Limine's page tables; it has no kernel-owned page-table manager, no heap, and no live frame-allocation callers. The descriptor setup reaches the shell in QEMU, but exception handlers have not had fault-injection testing.
- There is no scheduler, userspace, syscall ABI, persistent filesystem, user/kernel isolation, or general IRQ subsystem.

Never advance status or check off a roadmap item merely because source code or an interface exists. Update `docs/roadmap/README.md` only to reflect implementation and validation actually achieved.

## Source-of-truth documents

Consult the relevant documentation before modifying a subsystem:

- [`docs/architecture/drivers.md`](docs/architecture/drivers.md) — current driver scope and limitations.
- [`docs/security.md`](docs/security.md) — unsafe boundaries and security policy.
- [`docs/development/building.md`](docs/development/building.md) and [`docs/development/testing.md`](docs/development/testing.md) — supported commands and validation expectations.

When code and documentation disagree, inspect the implementation, resolve the discrepancy deliberately, and update the relevant documentation in the same change.

## Repository map

- `src/main.rs` — freestanding entry, boot snapshot acquisition, panic path, and shell handoff.
- `src/boot.rs` — mutable Limine requests, structural response/range validation, owned `BootInfo`, and boot diagnostics.
- `src/memory.rs` — allocation-free memory-map validation and known/unknown region classification.
- `src/frame.rs` — bounded physical-frame allocator core; it only uses validated `Usable` ranges, reserves the first MiB, and has fixed range metadata.
- `src/shell.rs` — serial line editor and kernel-side Crabshell executor.
- `src/vfs.rs` — fixed-capacity volatile RAM filesystem and host-side tests.
- `crates/crabshell/` — separate `no_std` parser crate. It has no terminal, filesystem, or kernel dependencies.
- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — polling COM1 driver for shell input/output.
- `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` — bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT, assembly stubs, and fatal exception diagnostics.
- `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` — CPUID identification and selected feature reporting.
- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — raw, non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling; not an input subsystem.
- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow port-I/O wrappers.
- `linker.ld`, `.cargo/config.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml` — target, linker, and toolchain configuration.
- `limine.conf`, `scripts/boot.py` — boot configuration and pinned image/emulator workflow.
- `justfile` — supported development commands.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — CI validation workflow.

## Engineering rules

### Keep changes incremental and coherent

1. Inspect the relevant source, tests, docs, and call sites before editing.
2. State assumptions, invariants, and failure behavior for new kernel interfaces.
3. Prefer small vertical slices that compile and can be tested over broad scaffolding or placeholder APIs.
4. Update tests and documentation alongside behavior changes.
5. Do not change unrelated code, rename files gratuitously, add speculative features, or rewrite project history.
6. Do not commit or create branches unless the user explicitly asks.

### Rust and dependency policy

- Preserve the kernel's `no_std`/freestanding constraints. Do not introduce `std` into kernel code.
- Prefer `core` and existing in-tree abstractions. Do not add third-party Rust dependencies without a concrete need and compatibility/security review.
- Keep the Crabshell parser independent of kernel I/O and VFS implementation. Kernel execution belongs in `src/shell.rs` or an appropriate kernel service.
- Do not add allocation-dependent APIs before a real heap exists. Fixed-capacity structures must document their limits and exhaustion behavior.
- Respect the workspace structure and the host-testable `rustix-kernel` library versus freestanding `rustix` binary boundary.

### Unsafe and hardware code

Unsafe code is expected only at explicit hardware, boot-protocol, assembly, or raw-memory boundaries. Keep each unsafe block narrow and document the invariant that makes it sound. Do not add broad `unsafe impl`, mutable global references, unchecked pointer arithmetic, or unreviewed inline/global assembly.

Before changing boot or memory code, account for these facts:

- Limine fills response pointers before `_start`; the request records must remain writable in the ELF image.
- Rustix validates nullness, alignment, counts, arithmetic, and physical ranges, but cannot prove that a non-null bootloader pointer is readable.
- Physical ranges are half-open `[start, end)` and must use checked arithmetic.
- Only regions classified `Usable` may enter the frame allocator. ACPI, bootloader-reclaimable, framebuffer, reserved, unknown, and other types are not free frames.
- A `Frame` is a physical address, not a dereferenceable pointer. Do not access it through the HHDM or change CR3 until an explicit, reviewed mapping policy and ownership proof exist.
- The kernel currently inherits Limine's page tables. Do not casually replace or mutate them: preserve the executing kernel, boot stack, `BootInfo`, request/response data, exception stacks, and mappings needed to continue execution.
- The exception setup is fatal-only. It does not enable maskable interrupts, configure a PIC/APIC, or provide recovery. Do not call `sti` or claim interrupt support without an IRQ design and tests.
- The shell and VFS run in ring 0 and are not isolated or secure.

For hardware changes, document assumptions about CPU mode, selectors, stacks, page permissions, interrupt state, and failure handling. Avoid new architecture mechanisms that cannot be statically reviewed or validated.

### Shell and filesystem contract

- Crabshell is presently a kernel-mode serial shell, not a userspace program or a POSIX shell.
- Its parser is a separate `no_std`, allocation-free crate; retain that boundary.
- The RAM filesystem is volatile and bounded. Preserve explicit errors and test capacity, path, and mutation edge cases.
- Do not imply persistence, permissions, links, process launching, or shell features that do not exist.
- Update the parser tests and `docs/architecture/crabshell.md` when adding or changing commands.

## Validation workflow

Run the narrowest relevant checks first, then broaden them. From the repository root, the supported commands are:

```sh
just fmt
just test
just check
just build
just image
just smoke
just verify
```

`just test` runs host-side library tests (memory-map validation, frame allocator, VFS, and Crabshell parser). `just check` checks `x86_64-unknown-none`; `just build` links the optimized ELF. `just verify` includes formatting, host tests, target check, pinned Limine image creation, and QEMU prompt smoke test. Image/boot checks need Python, `xorriso`, QEMU, the Rust target, and network access for the first pinned Limine download; Linux/WSL also needs `cc` to build Limine's host utility.

For changes to `src/main.rs`, `src/boot.rs`, linker/request configuration, `src/arch/x86_64/`, `src/frame.rs`, or paging/heap code, the intended full validation is `just verify`. If the environment does not permit a check, report the exact blocker and leave the corresponding roadmap criterion pending.

Do not claim a check passed unless it was run and its successful result was observed. Editor diagnostics are useful but are not a substitute for `cargo test`, a target build, or QEMU. A target check is not a final link; a linked ELF is not proof of boot; a prompt smoke test is not proof of interactive shell behavior or physical-hardware correctness.

## Completion criteria for agent changes

Before reporting work complete:

- Ensure source, tests, docs, and call sites agree.
- Review unsafe and hardware assumptions, including error paths and capacity limits.
- Run appropriate formatting/tests/build/boot checks, or clearly state why they could not run.
- Report files changed, behavior delivered, validation actually observed, and remaining risks.
- Keep milestone status accurate. A subsystem is not complete just because it has code.

    46	
    47	When code and documentation disagree, inspect the implementation, resolve the discrepancy deliberately, and update the relevant documentation in the same change.
    48	
    49	## Repository map
    50	
    51	- `src/main.rs` — freestanding entry, boot snapshot acquisition, panic path, and shell handoff.
    52	- `src/boot.rs` — mutable Limine requests, structural response/range validation, owned `BootInfo`, and boot diagnostics.
    53	- `src/memory.rs` — allocation-free memory-map validation and known/unknown region classification.
    54	- `src/frame.rs` — bounded physical-frame allocator core; it only uses validated `Usable` ranges, reserves the first MiB, and has fixed range metadata.
    55	- `src/shell.rs` — serial line editor and kernel-side Crabshell executor.
    56	- `src/vfs.rs` — fixed-capacity volatile RAM filesystem and host-side tests.
    57	- `crates/crabshell/` — separate `no_std` parser crate. It has no terminal, filesystem, or kernel dependencies.
    58	- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — polling COM1 driver for shell input/output.
    59	- `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` — bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT, assembly stubs, and fatal exception diagnostics.
    60	- `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` — CPUID identification and selected feature reporting.
    61	- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — raw, non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling; not an input subsystem.
    62	- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow port-I/O wrappers.
    63	- `linker.ld`, `.cargo/config.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml` — target, linker, and toolchain configuration.
    64	- `limine.conf`, `scripts/boot.py` — boot configuration and pinned image/emulator workflow.
    65	- `justfile` — supported development commands.
    66	- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — CI validation workflow.
    67	
    68	## Engineering rules
    69	
    70	### Keep changes incremental and coherent
    71	
    72	1. Inspect the relevant source, tests, docs, and call sites before editing.
    73	2. State assumptions, invariants, and failure behavior for new kernel interfaces.
    74	3. Prefer small vertical slices that compile and can be tested over broad scaffolding or placeholder APIs.
    75	4. Update tests and documentation alongside behavior changes.
    76	5. Do not change unrelated code, rename files gratuitously, add speculative features, or rewrite project history.
    77	6. Do not commit or create branches unless the user explicitly asks.
    78	
    79	### Rust and dependency policy
    80	
    81	- Preserve the kernel's `no_std`/freestanding constraints. Do not introduce `std` into kernel code.
    82	- Prefer `core` and existing in-tree abstractions. Do not add third-party Rust dependencies without a concrete need and compatibility/security review.
    83	- Keep the Crabshell parser independent of kernel I/O and VFS implementation. Kernel execution belongs in `src/shell.rs` or an appropriate kernel service.
    84	- Do not add allocation-dependent APIs before a real heap exists. Fixed-capacity structures must document their limits and exhaustion behavior.
    85	- Respect the workspace structure and the host-testable `rustix-kernel` library versus freestanding `rustix` binary boundary.
    86	
    87	### Unsafe and hardware code
    88	
    89	Unsafe code is expected only at explicit hardware, boot-protocol, assembly, or raw-memory boundaries. Keep each unsafe block narrow and document the invariant that makes it sound. Do not add broad `unsafe impl`, mutable global references, unchecked pointer arithmetic, or unreviewed inline/global assembly.
    90	
    91	Before changing boot or memory code, account for these facts:
    92	
    93	- Limine fills response pointers before `_start`; the request records must remain writable in the ELF image.
    94	- Rustix validates nullness, alignment, counts, arithmetic, and physical ranges, but cannot prove that a non-null bootloader pointer is readable.
    95	- Physical ranges are half-open `[start, end)` and must use checked arithmetic.
    96	- Only regions classified `Usable` may enter the frame allocator. ACPI, bootloader-reclaimable, framebuffer, reserved, unknown, and other types are not free frames.
    97	- A `Frame` is a physical address, not a dereferenceable pointer. Do not access it through the HHDM or change CR3 until an explicit, reviewed mapping policy and ownership proof exist.
    98	- The kernel currently inherits Limine's page tables. Do not casually replace or mutate them: preserve the executing kernel, boot stack, `BootInfo`, request/response data, exception stacks, and mappings needed to continue execution.
    99	- The exception setup is fatal-only. It does not enable maskable interrupts, configure a PIC/APIC, or provide recovery. Do not call `sti` or claim interrupt support without an IRQ design and tests.
   100	- The shell and VFS run in ring 0 and are not isolated or secure.
   101	
   102	For hardware changes, document assumptions about CPU mode, selectors, stacks, page permissions, interrupt state, and failure handling. Avoid new architecture mechanisms that cannot be statically reviewed or validated.
   103	
   104	### Shell and filesystem contract
   105	
   106	- Crabshell is presently a kernel-mode serial shell, not a userspace program or a POSIX shell.
   107	- Its parser is a separate `no_std`, allocation-free crate; retain that boundary.
   108	- The RAM filesystem is volatile and bounded. Preserve explicit errors and test capacity, path, and mutation edge cases.
   109	- Do not imply persistence, permissions, links, process launching, or shell features that do not exist.
   110	- Update the parser tests and `docs/architecture/crabshell.md` when adding or changing commands.
   111	
   112	## Validation workflow
   113	
   114	Run the narrowest relevant checks first, then broaden them. From the repository root, the supported commands are:
   115	
   116	```sh
   117	just fmt
   118	just test
   119	just check
   120	just build
   121	just image
   122	just smoke
   123	just verify
   124	```
   125	
   126	`just test` runs host-side library tests (memory-map validation, frame allocator, VFS, and Crabshell parser). `just check` checks `x86_64-unknown-none`; `just build` links the optimized ELF. `just verify` includes formatting, host tests, target check, pinned Limine image creation, and QEMU prompt smoke test. Image/boot checks need Python, `xorriso`, QEMU, the Rust target, and network access for the first pinned Limine download; Linux/WSL also needs `cc` to build Limine's host utility.
   127	
   128	For changes to `src/main.rs`, `src/boot.rs`, linker/request configuration, `src/arch/x86_64/`, `src/frame.rs`, or paging/heap code, the intended full validation is `just verify`. If the environment does not permit a check, report the exact blocker and leave the corresponding roadmap criterion pending.
   129	
   130	Do not claim a check passed unless it was run and its successful result was observed. Editor diagnostics are useful but are not a substitute for `cargo test`, a target build, or QEMU. A target check is not a final link; a linked ELF is not proof of boot; a prompt smoke test is not proof of interactive shell behavior or physical-hardware correctness.
   131	
   132	## Completion criteria for agent changes
   133	
   134	Before reporting work complete:
   135	
   136	- Ensure source, tests, docs, and call sites agree.
   137	- Review unsafe and hardware assumptions, including error paths and capacity limits.
   138	- Run appropriate formatting/tests/build/boot checks, or clearly state why they could not run.
   139	- Report files changed, behavior delivered, validation actually observed, and remaining risks.
   140	- Keep milestone status accurate. A subsystem is not complete just because it has code.

    11	pub const fn is_canonical_virtual_address(address: u64, address_bits: u8) -> bool {

    14	    }

    23	    } else {
    24	        u64::MAX >> address_bits
    25	    };
    26	    upper_bits == expected_upper_bits
    27	}

   154	    pub fn push(&mut self, base: u64, length: u64, raw_kind: u64) -> Result<(), MemoryMapError> {
   155	        let index = self.map.region_count;
   156	        if index == MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
   157	            return Err(MemoryMapError::TooManyRegions);
   158	        }
   159	        if length == 0 {
   160	            return Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyRegion { index });
   161	        }
   162	        let end = base
   163	            .checked_add(length)
   164	            .ok_or(MemoryMapError::AddressOverflow { index })?;
   165	        let kind = RegionKind::from_limine(raw_kind);
   166	
   167	        for (other_index, other) in self.map.regions().iter().enumerate() {
   168	            if base < other.end && other.start < end {
   169	                return Err(MemoryMapError::OverlappingRegions {
   170	                    first: other_index,
   171	                    second: index,
   172	                });
   173	            }
   174	        }
   175	
   176	        let usable_bytes = if kind == RegionKind::Usable {
   177	            self.map
   178	                .usable_bytes
   179	                .checked_add(length)
   180	                .ok_or(MemoryMapError::UsableTotalOverflow)?
   181	        } else {
   182	            self.map.usable_bytes
   183	        };
   184	
   185	        self.map.regions[index] = PhysicalRegion {
   186	            start: base,
   187	            end,
   188	            kind,
   189	        };
   190	        self.map.region_count += 1;
   191	        self.map.usable_bytes = usable_bytes;

   176	    }

   255	        cpu.physical_address_bits,
   256	        cpu.max_linear_address_bits,
   257	        cpu.active_linear_address_bits,
   258	        cpu.active_linear_address_bits == 57

   261	
   262	fn is_valid_pointer<T>(pointer: *const T, virtual_address_bits: u8) -> bool {
   263	    let start = pointer as usize;
   264	    let Some(end) = start.checked_add(size_of::<T>()) else {
   265	        return false;
   266	    };
   267	    !pointer.is_null()
   268	        && start & (align_of::<T>() - 1) == 0
   269	        && is_canonical_virtual_address(start as u64, virtual_address_bits)
   270	        && is_canonical_virtual_address((end - 1) as u64, virtual_address_bits)
   271	}

     2	
     3	use core::arch::asm;
     4	use core::arch::x86_64::{__cpuid, __cpuid_count};
     5	
     6	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
     7	pub struct CpuInfo {
     8	    pub vendor: [u8; 12],
     9	    pub max_basic_leaf: u32,
    10	    pub max_extended_leaf: u32,
    11	    pub has_sse2: bool,
    12	    pub has_nx: bool,
    13	    pub has_1g_pages: bool,
    14	    pub has_long_mode: bool,
    15	    pub has_la57: bool,
    16	    pub physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    17	    pub max_linear_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    18	    pub active_linear_address_bits: u8,
    19	}
    20	
    21	/// Read CPUID identity and a small set of baseline kernel-relevant features.
    22	pub fn identify() -> CpuInfo {
    23	    // CPUID is part of the x86_64 architectural baseline.
    24	    let basic = __cpuid(0);
    25	    let mut vendor = [0; 12];
    26	    vendor[0..4].copy_from_slice(&basic.ebx.to_le_bytes());
    27	    vendor[4..8].copy_from_slice(&basic.edx.to_le_bytes());
    28	    vendor[8..12].copy_from_slice(&basic.ecx.to_le_bytes());
    29	
    30	    let basic_features = if basic.eax >= 1 {
    31	        Some(__cpuid(1))
    32	    } else {
    33	        None
    34	    };
    35	    let extended = __cpuid(0x8000_0000);
    36	    let extended_features = if extended.eax >= 0x8000_0001 {
    37	        Some(__cpuid(0x8000_0001))
    38	    } else {
    39	        None
    40	    };
    41	    let structured_features = if basic.eax >= 7 {
    42	        Some(__cpuid_count(7, 0))
    43	    } else {
    44	        None
    45	    };
    46	    let address_widths = if extended.eax >= 0x8000_0008 {
    47	        Some(__cpuid(0x8000_0008).eax)
    48	    } else {
    49	        None
    50	    };
    51	
    52	    CpuInfo {
    53	        vendor,
    54	        max_basic_leaf: basic.eax,
    55	        max_extended_leaf: extended.eax,
    56	        has_sse2: basic_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 26) != 0),
    57	        has_nx: extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 20) != 0),
    58	        has_1g_pages: extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 26) != 0),
    59	        has_long_mode: extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 29) != 0),
    60	        has_la57: structured_features.is_some_and(|features| features.ecx & (1 << 16) != 0),
    61	        physical_address_bits: address_widths.map(|eax| (eax & 0xff) as u8),
    62	        max_linear_address_bits: address_widths.map(|eax| ((eax >> 8) & 0xff) as u8),
    63	        active_linear_address_bits: active_linear_address_bits(),
    64	    }
    65	}
    66	
    67	/// Read the active linear-address width from CR4.LA57 without changing paging.
    68	pub fn active_linear_address_bits() -> u8 {
    69	    let cr4: u64;
    70	    // SAFETY: Rustix runs at CPL 0; reading CR4 is a privileged, non-mutating operation.
    71	    unsafe { asm!("mov {}, cr4", out(reg) cr4, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
    72	    if cr4 & (1 << 12) != 0 {
    73	        57
    74	    } else {
    75	        48
    76	    }
    77	}

     1	# Memory-management direction
     2	
     3	## What exists now
     4	
     5	`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation and classification. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.
     6	
     7	`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and coalesces adjacent free ranges. The ownership contract assumes one allocator instance per physical map: within that instance, each eligible frame is owned either by its free-range table or by a non-copyable `Frame` token while allocated. The public constructor does not enforce unique instances, so callers must not initialize multiple allocators for the same physical map; the current boot path retains one allocator in `BootInfo`. `allocate` returns `None` when no free frame remains. `deallocate` consumes the token only on success; on any error, including free-range-table exhaustion, it returns a `DeallocationError` containing the original token and leaves allocator state unchanged. The range tables each have a fixed `MAX_FRAME_RANGES` capacity, so fragmentation can prevent a frame from being returned until nearby ranges coalesce. No kernel service currently allocates frames for mappings or other work.
     8	
     9	`Frame::address()` is a physical address value, not a dereferenceable pointer and not a proof that the frame is mapped. CPU diagnostics now read `CR4.LA57` to report the active linear-address width (48 or 57 bits) and query `CPUID.80000008H` for physical and maximum linear-address widths when available. Boot-protocol pointers are checked against the active width, with host tests for 48- and 57-bit canonical boundaries. These facts do not prove that any physical address is mapped.
    10	
    11	The requested Limine base revision is 3. Its protocol maps only `Usable`, `BootloaderReclaimable`, `ExecutableAndModules`, and `Framebuffer` memory-map regions into the HHDM; reserved, ACPI, bad, and unknown regions are not in that mapping set. HHDM mappings use at least 4 KiB granularity and may cover page-aligned bytes beyond unaligned region boundaries. On x86_64, inherited HHDM mappings are supervisor RWX, normally write-back cached, with framebuffer mappings write-combining when PAT is available. Therefore an HHDM offset is not a blanket physical-memory access grant, and inherited HHDM permissions are not Rustix's future W^X policy. See the [Limine base revision 3 protocol](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine-protocol/blob/trunk/PROTOCOL.md#base-revision-3) and its memory-layout/caching sections.
    12	
    13	Rustix still does not use the HHDM to access physical memory or validate translated physical ranges against the reported physical-address width. A future mapping policy must check physical bounds, checked `offset + address` arithmetic, active-width canonicality, and the memory-map types whose pages Limine guarantees mapped before it dereferences any HHDM address. Rustix-owned mappings should be non-executable by default; executable kernel text must be explicit. MMIO requires an explicit device range and cache policy, and guard regions must remain unmapped. A page-table transition must preserve the kernel image, active stacks, boot data, descriptor tables, and any loader mappings still needed. Rustix does not reclaim bootloader memory, own or replace the inherited Limine page tables, or provide a heap. Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup and fatal exception diagnostics live in `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs`; they do not enable maskable IRQs.
    14	
    15	## Planned memory layers
    16	
    17	1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
    18	2. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; add real allocation callers only after the page-mapping policy and ownership rules are implemented.
    19	3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix still runs on inherited Limine page tables. Before replacing them, preserve the executing kernel, bootstrap/Ring-0 stacks, request/response data, and exception stacks; define the HHDM extent and explicit mapping permissions/cache attributes. Keep writable-executable mappings disallowed by default and reserve MMIO and guard regions.
    20	4. **Heap:** add a global allocator only after frame allocation and page mapping are initialized. Define allocation failure behavior for kernel and interrupt contexts.
    21	5. **Process address spaces:** isolate userspace; define copy-in/copy-out helpers and never treat user pointers as kernel references.
    22	
    23	## Invariants to preserve
    24	
    25	- Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
    26	- Only complete frames in validated `Usable` regions enter the allocator; the first MiB remains reserved. Firmware and loader-reclaimable regions are not silently promoted to free memory.
    27	- Under the single-allocator-per-physical-map contract, a frame is represented by one allocator-free range or one caller-owned, non-copyable `Frame` token. Only a successful `deallocate` transfers the token back to the allocator; errors return the token and leave allocator ranges and accounting unchanged. The current public constructor relies on callers to enforce unique allocator instances.
    28	- `allocate` returns `None` on frame exhaustion. Metadata-capacity exhaustion is an explicit error, never silent loss of a frame.
    29	- A `Frame` address is physical, not directly dereferenceable. No HHDM translation, page-table mutation, or CR3 switch is permitted until address widths, mapping coverage, permissions/cache attributes, and transition-preservation requirements are established.
    30	- Mapping changes validate alignment, canonical addresses, ownership, and permissions before touching tables.
    31	- User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
    32	- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, exhaustion, and unchanged state/ownership on failure.
    33	
    34	These are design requirements for future milestones, not functionality delivered by the current boot summary.

//! Allocation-free validation for virtual addresses and physical memory maps.

/// Limine's memory-map type for ordinary usable RAM.
pub const MEMORY_MAP_USABLE: u64 = 0;
/// Maximum number of memory regions retained in the boot snapshot.
pub const MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS: usize = 256;

/// Check whether an address is canonical for a sign-extended virtual width.
///
/// Widths outside `1..=64` are rejected. A 64-bit width accepts every address.
pub const fn is_canonical_virtual_address(address: u64, address_bits: u8) -> bool {
    if address_bits == 0 || address_bits > 64 {
        return false;
    }
    if address_bits == 64 {
        return true;
    }

    let sign_bit = (address >> (address_bits - 1)) & 1;
    let upper_bits = address >> address_bits;
    let expected_upper_bits = if sign_bit == 0 {
        0
    } else {
        u64::MAX >> address_bits
    };
    upper_bits == expected_upper_bits
}

/// Check that a non-empty half-open physical range fits an address width.
pub const fn physical_range_fits_address_width(
    start: u64,
    end: u64,
    address_bits: u8,
) -> bool {
    if start >= end || address_bits == 0 || address_bits > 64 {
        return false;
    }
    address_bits == 64 || end <= (1u64 << address_bits)
}

/// Validate the page-rounded HHDM span for one Limine base-revision-3 region.
///
/// `physical_bits` is `None` only when CPUID does not report the width. This
/// checks arithmetic and canonicality, not whether the inherited page tables
/// actually contain the mapping.
pub const fn limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
    offset: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    physical_end: u64,
    physical_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_bits: u8,
) -> bool {
    const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;
    const PAGE_MASK: u64 = !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);

    if physical_start >= physical_end
        || offset & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
        || (virtual_bits != 48 && virtual_bits != 57)
    {
        return false;
    }
    if let Some(bits) = physical_bits {
        if !physical_range_fits_address_width(physical_start, physical_end, bits) {
            return false;
        }
    }

    let mapped_start = physical_start & PAGE_MASK;
    let Some(rounded_end) = physical_end.checked_add(PAGE_SIZE - 1) else {
        return false;
    };
    let mapped_end = rounded_end & PAGE_MASK;
    if mapped_start >= mapped_end {
        return false;
    }
    if let Some(bits) = physical_bits {
        if !physical_range_fits_address_width(mapped_start, mapped_end, bits) {
            return false;
        }
    }

    let Some(virtual_start) = offset.checked_add(mapped_start) else {
        return false;
    };
    let Some(virtual_last) = offset.checked_add(mapped_end - 1) else {
        return false;
    };
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(virtual_start, virtual_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address(virtual_last, virtual_bits)
    {
        return false;
    }

    let sign_bit = 1u64 << (virtual_bits - 1);
    virtual_start & sign_bit == virtual_last & sign_bit
}

/// Classification of a physical memory region from the Limine memory map.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RegionKind {
    Usable,
    Reserved,
    AcpiReclaimable,
    AcpiNvs,
    BadMemory,
    BootloaderReclaimable,
    ExecutableAndModules,
    Framebuffer,
    Unknown(u64),
}

impl RegionKind {
    /// Whether Limine base revision 3 includes this type in the HHDM.
    pub const fn is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm(self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self,
            Self::Usable
                | Self::BootloaderReclaimable
                | Self::ExecutableAndModules
                | Self::Framebuffer
        )
    }

    const fn from_limine(kind: u64) -> Self {
        match kind {
            0 => Self::Usable,
            1 => Self::Reserved,
            2 => Self::AcpiReclaimable,
            3 => Self::AcpiNvs,
            4 => Self::BadMemory,
            5 => Self::BootloaderReclaimable,
            6 => Self::ExecutableAndModules,
            7 => Self::Framebuffer,
            unknown => Self::Unknown(unknown),
        }
    }
}

/// Unvalidated region fields copied from a boot protocol response.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RawMemoryRegion {
    pub base: u64,
    pub length: u64,
    pub kind: u64,
}

/// Validated half-open physical address range `[start, end)`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PhysicalRegion {
    start: u64,
    end: u64,
    kind: RegionKind,
}

impl PhysicalRegion {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        start: 0,
        end: 0,
        kind: RegionKind::Unknown(0),
    };

    pub const fn start(&self) -> u64 {
        self.start
    }

    pub const fn end(&self) -> u64 {
        self.end
    }

    pub const fn length(&self) -> u64 {
        self.end - self.start
    }

    pub const fn kind(&self) -> RegionKind {
        self.kind
    }
}

/// Errors produced when a memory map is malformed or exceeds kernel capacity.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MemoryMapError {
    EmptyMap,
    TooManyRegions,
    EmptyRegion { index: usize },
    AddressOverflow { index: usize },
    OverlappingRegions { first: usize, second: usize },
    UsableTotalOverflow,
}

/// Validated, allocation-free snapshot of the physical memory map.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MemoryMap {
    regions: [PhysicalRegion; MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS],
    region_count: usize,
    usable_bytes: u64,
}

impl MemoryMap {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        regions: [PhysicalRegion::EMPTY; MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS],
        region_count: 0,
        usable_bytes: 0,
    };

    pub fn from_raw(regions: &[RawMemoryRegion]) -> Result<Self, MemoryMapError> {
        let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
        for region in regions {
            builder.push(region.base, region.length, region.kind)?;
        }
        builder.finish()
    }

    pub fn regions(&self) -> &[PhysicalRegion] {
        &self.regions[..self.region_count]
    }

    pub const fn usable_bytes(&self) -> u64 {
        self.usable_bytes
    }
}

/// Incremental validator used to copy loader entries without an intermediate heap.
pub struct MemoryMapBuilder {
    map: MemoryMap,
}

impl MemoryMapBuilder {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            map: MemoryMap::EMPTY,
        }
    }

    pub fn push(&mut self, base: u64, length: u64, raw_kind: u64) -> Result<(), MemoryMapError> {
        let index = self.map.region_count;
        if index == MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
            return Err(MemoryMapError::TooManyRegions);
        }
        if length == 0 {
            return Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyRegion { index });
        }
        let end = base
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(MemoryMapError::AddressOverflow { index })?;
        let kind = RegionKind::from_limine(raw_kind);

        for (other_index, other) in self.map.regions().iter().enumerate() {
            if base < other.end && other.start < end {
                return Err(MemoryMapError::OverlappingRegions {
                    first: other_index,
                    second: index,
                });
            }
        }

        let usable_bytes = if kind == RegionKind::Usable {
            self.map
                .usable_bytes
                .checked_add(length)
                .ok_or(MemoryMapError::UsableTotalOverflow)?
        } else {
            self.map.usable_bytes
        };

        self.map.regions[index] = PhysicalRegion {
            start: base,
            end,
            kind,
        };
        self.map.region_count += 1;
        self.map.usable_bytes = usable_bytes;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn finish(self) -> Result<MemoryMap, MemoryMapError> {
        if self.map.region_count == 0 {
            Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyMap)
        } else {
            Ok(self.map)
        }
    }
}

impl Default for MemoryMapBuilder {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// Add an already-validated usable region length to a running total.
///
/// Non-usable regions leave the total unchanged. `None` signals arithmetic
/// overflow so callers can report malformed or unrepresentable maps.
pub const fn add_usable_bytes(total: u64, region_kind: u64, region_length: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    if region_kind == MEMORY_MAP_USABLE {
        total.checked_add(region_length)
    } else {
        Some(total)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use core::assert_eq;

    use super::{
        add_usable_bytes, is_canonical_virtual_address, limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid,
        physical_range_fits_address_width, MemoryMap, MemoryMapBuilder, MemoryMapError,
        RawMemoryRegion, RegionKind, MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS, MEMORY_MAP_USABLE,
    };

    #[test]
    fn canonical_virtual_addresses_follow_the_selected_width() {
        assert!(is_canonical_virtual_address(0x0000_7fff_ffff_ffff, 48));
        assert!(!is_canonical_virtual_address(0x0000_8000_0000_0000, 48));
        assert!(is_canonical_virtual_address(0xffff_8000_0000_0000, 48));
        assert!(!is_canonical_virtual_address(0xffff_7fff_ffff_ffff, 48));

        assert!(is_canonical_virtual_address(0x00ff_ffff_ffff_ffff, 57));
        assert!(!is_canonical_virtual_address(0x0100_0000_0000_0000, 57));
        assert!(is_canonical_virtual_address(0xff00_0000_0000_0000, 57));
        assert!(!is_canonical_virtual_address(0xfeff_ffff_ffff_ffff, 57));
        assert!(!is_canonical_virtual_address(0, 0));
        assert!(!is_canonical_virtual_address(0, 65));
    }

    #[test]
    fn physical_ranges_fit_the_reported_address_width() {
        assert!(physical_range_fits_address_width(0x1000, 1 << 40, 40));
        assert!(!physical_range_fits_address_width(0x1000, (1 << 40) + 1, 40));
        assert!(!physical_range_fits_address_width(1, 1, 40));
        assert!(!physical_range_fits_address_width(0, 1, 0));
        assert!(!physical_range_fits_address_width(0, 1, 65));
        assert!(physical_range_fits_address_width(u64::MAX - 1, u64::MAX, 64));
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_page_rounded_limine_hhdm_ranges_without_accessing_them() {
        let offset = 0xffff_8000_0000_0000;
        assert!(limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
            offset,
            0x1234,
            0x2345,
            Some(40),
            48
        ));
        assert!(!limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
            offset,
            0x1234,
            (1 << 40) + 1,
            Some(40),
            48
        ));
        assert!(!limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
            u64::MAX - 0x0fff,
            0x1000,
            0x2000,
            None,
            48
        ));
        assert!(!limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
            0x0000_8000_0000_0000,
            0x1000,
            0x2000,
            None,
            48
        ));
        assert!(!limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
            0,
            0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000,
            0x0000_8000_0000_1000,
            Some(64),
            48
        ));
        assert!(!limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(offset, 0x1000, 0x2000, None, 46));
    }

    #[test]
    fn classifies_limine_v3_hhdm_region_types() {
        assert!(RegionKind::Usable.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(RegionKind::ExecutableAndModules.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(RegionKind::Framebuffer.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(!RegionKind::Reserved.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(!RegionKind::AcpiReclaimable.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(!RegionKind::AcpiNvs.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(!RegionKind::BadMemory.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(!RegionKind::Unknown(99).is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
    }

    #[test]
    fn counts_only_usable_regions() {
        assert_eq!(add_usable_bytes(4096, MEMORY_MAP_USABLE, 2048), Some(6144));
        assert_eq!(add_usable_bytes(4096, 1, 2048), Some(4096));
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_total_overflow() {
        assert_eq!(add_usable_bytes(u64::MAX - 4, MEMORY_MAP_USABLE, 8), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_ranges_and_preserves_all_region_kinds() {
        let raw = [
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x1000,
                length: 0x2000,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x4000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 5,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x5000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 99,
            },
        ];
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&raw).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(map.usable_bytes(), 0x2000);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[0].start(), 0x1000);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[0].end(), 0x3000);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[0].length(), 0x2000);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[0].kind(), RegionKind::Usable);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[1].kind(), RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[2].kind(), RegionKind::Unknown(99));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_empty_zero_length_overflowing_and_overlapping_maps() {
        assert_eq!(MemoryMap::from_raw(&[]), Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyMap));
        assert_eq!(
            MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0,
                length: 0,
                kind: 0
            }]),
            Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyRegion { index: 0 })
        );
        let overflowing = [RawMemoryRegion {
            base: u64::MAX - 3,
            length: 8,
            kind: 0,
        }];
        assert_eq!(
            MemoryMap::from_raw(&overflowing),
            Err(MemoryMapError::AddressOverflow { index: 0 })
        );

        let overlap = [
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x1000,
                length: 0x2000,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x2fff,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 1,
            },
        ];
        assert_eq!(
            MemoryMap::from_raw(&overlap),
            Err(MemoryMapError::OverlappingRegions {
                first: 0,
                second: 1
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn accepts_adjacent_ranges_and_rejects_excess_entries() {
        let adjacent = [
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x1000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x2000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 1,
            },
        ];
        assert!(MemoryMap::from_raw(&adjacent).is_ok());

        let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
        for index in 0..MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
            builder.push((index as u64) * 0x2000, 0x1000, 1).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(
            builder.push(0x1_0000_0000, 0x1000, 1),
            Err(MemoryMapError::TooManyRegions)
        );
    }
}

/// Owned kernel snapshot of the handoff values Rustix currently consumes.
pub struct BootInfo {
    pub hhdm_revision: u64,
    pub hhdm_offset: u64,
    pub memory_map_revision: u64,
    pub memory_map: MemoryMap,
    pub frame_allocator: FrameAllocator,
    pub cpu_info: crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BootInfoError {
    MissingHhdmResponse,
    InvalidHhdmResponsePointer,
    InvalidHhdmOffset,
    MissingMemoryMapResponse,
    InvalidMemoryMapResponsePointer,
    MemoryMapCountDoesNotFit,
    TooManyMemoryRegions,
    EmptyMemoryMap,
    InvalidEntriesPointer,
    EntriesAddressOverflow,
    InvalidEntryPointer { index: usize },
    InvalidPhysicalRange { index: usize },
    InvalidHhdmMappingRange { index: usize },
    InvalidMemoryMap(MemoryMapError),
    FrameAllocator(FrameError),
}

/// Copy and validate the boot data needed by the current kernel.
///
/// Structural checks can reject malformed pointers and ranges, but cannot prove
/// that a loader-provided pointer is mapped and readable. That remains part of
/// the documented Limine handoff trust boundary until the kernel owns its maps.
pub fn capture_boot_information() -> Result<BootInfo, BootInfoError> {
    let cpu_info = crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::identify();
    let virtual_address_bits = cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits;
    let hhdm_request = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(HHDM_REQUEST);
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let hhdm_pointer =
        unsafe { core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*hhdm_request).response)) };
    if hhdm_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingHhdmResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(hhdm_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: The Limine response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable
    // response object; its nullness and alignment are checked above.
    let hhdm = unsafe { hhdm_pointer.read_volatile() };
    if hhdm.offset & 0xfff != 0 || !is_canonical_virtual_address(hhdm.offset, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmOffset);
    }

    let memory_map_request = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(MEMORY_MAP_REQUEST);
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let memory_map_pointer =
        unsafe { core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*memory_map_request).response)) };
    if memory_map_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingMemoryMapResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(memory_map_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMapResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: The Limine response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable
    // response object; its nullness and alignment are checked above.
    let response = unsafe { memory_map_pointer.read_volatile() };
    let entry_count = usize::try_from(response.entry_count)
        .map_err(|_| BootInfoError::MemoryMapCountDoesNotFit)?;
    if entry_count > MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
        return Err(BootInfoError::TooManyMemoryRegions);
    }
    if entry_count == 0 {
        return Err(BootInfoError::EmptyMemoryMap);
    }
    if response.entries.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(response.entries, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }
    let entry_bytes = entry_count
        .checked_mul(size_of::<*const MemoryMapEntry>())
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::EntriesAddressOverflow)?;
    let entries_start = response.entries as usize;
    let entries_end = entries_start
        .checked_add(entry_bytes)
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::EntriesAddressOverflow)?;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(entries_start as u64, virtual_address_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address((entries_end - 1) as u64, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }

    let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
    for index in 0..entry_count {
        // SAFETY: Limine promises an array of `entry_count` pointers. The count
        // is capped and pointer alignment/address arithmetic are checked above.
        let entry_pointer = unsafe { response.entries.add(index).read_volatile() };
        if !is_valid_pointer(entry_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
            return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntryPointer { index });
        }
        // SAFETY: Limine promises each non-null entry pointer is readable.
        let entry = unsafe { entry_pointer.read_volatile() };
        builder
            .push(entry.base, entry.length, entry.kind)
            .map_err(BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMap)?;
    }

    let memory_map = builder.finish().map_err(|error| match error {
        MemoryMapError::EmptyMap => BootInfoError::EmptyMemoryMap,
        other => BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMap(other),
    })?;
    for (index, region) in memory_map.regions().iter().enumerate() {
        if let Some(physical_bits) = cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
            if !physical_range_fits_address_width(region.start(), region.end(), physical_bits) {
                return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidPhysicalRange { index });
            }
        }
        if region.kind().is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm()
            && !limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
                hhdm.offset,
                region.start(),
                region.end(),
                cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
                virtual_address_bits,
            )
        {
            return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmMappingRange { index });
        }
    }
    let frame_allocator =
        FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&memory_map).map_err(BootInfoError::FrameAllocator)?;

    Ok(BootInfo {
        hhdm_revision: hhdm.revision,
        hhdm_offset: hhdm.offset,
        memory_map_revision: response.revision,
        memory_map,
        frame_allocator,
        cpu_info,
    })
}

/// Print a report from the copied snapshot; no loader pointers are used here.
pub fn report_boot_information(boot_info: &BootInfo) {
    crate::kprintln!(
        "HHDM: offset {:#018x}, response revision {}",
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.hhdm_revision
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "memory map: {} validated regions, {} MiB usable RAM, response revision {}",
        boot_info.memory_map.regions().len(),
        boot_info.memory_map.usable_bytes() / (1024 * 1024),
        boot_info.memory_map_revision
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "physical frames: {} managed, {} free (4 KiB each)",
        boot_info.frame_allocator.managed_frames(),
        boot_info.frame_allocator.free_frames()
    );
    for region in boot_info.memory_map.regions() {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "  [{:#018x}, {:#018x}) {:?}",
            region.start(),
            region.end(),
            region.kind()
        );
    }
    crate::kprintln!("console: COM1 serial (polling)");

    let cpu = &boot_info.cpu_info;
    let vendor = core::str::from_utf8(&cpu.vendor).unwrap_or("unknown");
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU: {} (basic leaf {}, extended leaf {:#x})",
        vendor,
        cpu.max_basic_leaf,
        cpu.max_extended_leaf
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU feature support: SSE2={}, NX={}, 1GiB-pages={}, long-mode={}, LA57-supported={}",
        cpu.has_sse2,
        cpu.has_nx,
        cpu.has_1g_pages,
        cpu.has_long_mode,
        cpu.has_la57
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU address widths (bits): physical={:?}, max-linear={:?}, active-linear={} (LA57 active={})",
        cpu.physical_address_bits,
        cpu.max_linear_address_bits,
        cpu.active_linear_address_bits,
        cpu.active_linear_address_bits == 57
    );
}

fn is_valid_pointer<T>(pointer: *const T, virtual_address_bits: u8) -> bool {
    let start = pointer as usize;
    let Some(end) = start.checked_add(size_of::<T>()) else {
        return false;
    };
    !pointer.is_null()
        && start & (align_of::<T>() - 1) == 0
        && is_canonical_virtual_address(start as u64, virtual_address_bits)
        && is_canonical_virtual_address((end - 1) as u64, virtual_address_bits)
}

/// Owned kernel snapshot of the handoff values Rustix currently consumes.
pub struct BootInfo {

    pub hhdm_offset: u64,
    pub memory_map_revision: u64,
    pub memory_map: MemoryMap,
    pub frame_allocator: FrameAllocator,
    pub cpu_info: crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BootInfoError {
    MissingHhdmResponse,
    InvalidHhdmResponsePointer,
    InvalidHhdmOffset,
    MissingMemoryMapResponse,
    InvalidMemoryMapResponsePointer,
    MemoryMapCountDoesNotFit,
    TooManyMemoryRegions,
    EmptyMemoryMap,
    InvalidEntriesPointer,
    EntriesAddressOverflow,
    InvalidEntryPointer { index: usize },
    InvalidPhysicalRange { index: usize },
    InvalidHhdmMappingRange { index: usize },
    InvalidMemoryMap(MemoryMapError),
    FrameAllocator(FrameError),
}

/// Copy and validate the boot data needed by the current kernel.
///
/// Structural checks can reject malformed pointers and ranges, but cannot prove
/// that a loader-provided pointer is mapped and readable. That remains part of
/// the documented Limine handoff trust boundary until the kernel owns its maps.
pub fn capture_boot_information() -> Result<BootInfo, BootInfoError> {
    let cpu_info = crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::identify();
    let virtual_address_bits = cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits;
    let hhdm_request = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(HHDM_REQUEST);
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let hhdm_pointer =
        unsafe { core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*hhdm_request).response)) };
    if hhdm_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingHhdmResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(hhdm_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: The Limine response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable
    // response object; its nullness and alignment are checked above.
    let hhdm = unsafe { hhdm_pointer.read_volatile() };
    if hhdm.offset & 0xfff != 0 || !is_canonical_virtual_address(hhdm.offset, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmOffset);
    }

    let memory_map_request = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(MEMORY_MAP_REQUEST);
    // SAFETY: Limine has completed writing the request response before `_start`.
    let memory_map_pointer =
        unsafe { core::ptr::read_volatile(core::ptr::addr_of!((*memory_map_request).response)) };
    if memory_map_pointer.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::MissingMemoryMapResponse);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(memory_map_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMapResponsePointer);
    }
    // SAFETY: The Limine response pointer is trusted to refer to a readable
    // response object; its nullness and alignment are checked above.
    let response = unsafe { memory_map_pointer.read_volatile() };
    let entry_count = usize::try_from(response.entry_count)
        .map_err(|_| BootInfoError::MemoryMapCountDoesNotFit)?;
    if entry_count > MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
        return Err(BootInfoError::TooManyMemoryRegions);
    }
    if entry_count == 0 {
        return Err(BootInfoError::EmptyMemoryMap);
    }
    if response.entries.is_null() {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }
    if !is_valid_pointer(response.entries, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }
    let entry_bytes = entry_count
        .checked_mul(size_of::<*const MemoryMapEntry>())
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::EntriesAddressOverflow)?;
    let entries_start = response.entries as usize;
    let entries_end = entries_start
        .checked_add(entry_bytes)
        .ok_or(BootInfoError::EntriesAddressOverflow)?;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(entries_start as u64, virtual_address_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address((entries_end - 1) as u64, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntriesPointer);
    }

    let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
    for index in 0..entry_count {
        // SAFETY: Limine promises an array of `entry_count` pointers. The count
        // is capped and pointer alignment/address arithmetic are checked above.
        let entry_pointer = unsafe { response.entries.add(index).read_volatile() };
        if !is_valid_pointer(entry_pointer, virtual_address_bits) {
            return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidEntryPointer { index });
        }
        // SAFETY: Limine promises each non-null entry pointer is readable.
        let entry = unsafe { entry_pointer.read_volatile() };
        builder
            .push(entry.base, entry.length, entry.kind)
            .map_err(BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMap)?;
    }

    let memory_map = builder.finish().map_err(|error| match error {
        MemoryMapError::EmptyMap => BootInfoError::EmptyMemoryMap,
        other => BootInfoError::InvalidMemoryMap(other),
    })?;
    for (index, region) in memory_map.regions().iter().enumerate() {
        if let Some(physical_bits) = cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
            if !physical_range_fits_address_width(region.start(), region.end(), physical_bits) {
                return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidPhysicalRange { index });
            }
        }
        if region.kind().is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm()
            && !limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
                hhdm.offset,
                region.start(),
                region.end(),
                cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
                virtual_address_bits,
            )
        {
            return Err(BootInfoError::InvalidHhdmMappingRange { index });
        }
    }
    let frame_allocator =
        FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&memory_map).map_err(BootInfoError::FrameAllocator)?;

    Ok(BootInfo {
        hhdm_revision: hhdm.revision,
        hhdm_offset: hhdm.offset,
        memory_map_revision: response.revision,
        memory_map,
        frame_allocator,
        cpu_info,
    })
}

/// Print a report from the copied snapshot; no loader pointers are used here.
pub fn report_boot_information(boot_info: &BootInfo) {
    crate::kprintln!(
        "HHDM: offset {:#018x}, response revision {}",
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.hhdm_revision
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "memory map: {} validated regions, {} MiB usable RAM, response revision {}",
        boot_info.memory_map.regions().len(),
        boot_info.memory_map.usable_bytes() / (1024 * 1024),
        boot_info.memory_map_revision
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "physical frames: {} managed, {} free (4 KiB each)",
        boot_info.frame_allocator.managed_frames(),
        boot_info.frame_allocator.free_frames()
    );
    for region in boot_info.memory_map.regions() {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "  [{:#018x}, {:#018x}) {:?}",
            region.start(),
            region.end(),
            region.kind()
        );
    }
    crate::kprintln!("console: COM1 serial (polling)");

    let cpu = &boot_info.cpu_info;
    let vendor = core::str::from_utf8(&cpu.vendor).unwrap_or("unknown");
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU: {} (basic leaf {}, extended leaf {:#x})",
        vendor,
        cpu.max_basic_leaf,
        cpu.max_extended_leaf
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU feature support: SSE2={}, NX={}, 1GiB-pages={}, long-mode={}, LA57-supported={}",
        cpu.has_sse2,
        cpu.has_nx,
        cpu.has_1g_pages,
        cpu.has_long_mode,
        cpu.has_la57
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU address widths (bits): physical={:?}, max-linear={:?}, active-linear={} (LA57 active={})",
        cpu.physical_address_bits,
        cpu.max_linear_address_bits,
        cpu.active_linear_address_bits,
        cpu.active_linear_address_bits == 57
    );
}

fn is_valid_pointer<T>(pointer: *const T, virtual_address_bits: u8) -> bool {
    let start = pointer as usize;
    let Some(end) = start.checked_add(size_of::<T>()) else {
        return false;
    };
    !pointer.is_null()
        && start & (align_of::<T>() - 1) == 0
        && is_canonical_virtual_address(start as u64, virtual_address_bits)
        && is_canonical_virtual_address((end - 1) as u64, virtual_address_bits)
}

pub fn report_boot_information(boot_info: &BootInfo) {
    crate::kprintln!(
        "HHDM: offset {:#018x}, response revision {}",
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.hhdm_revision
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "memory map: {} validated regions, {} MiB usable RAM, response revision {}",
        boot_info.memory_map.regions().len(),
        boot_info.memory_map.usable_bytes() / (1024 * 1024),
        boot_info.memory_map_revision
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "physical frames: {} managed, {} free (4 KiB each)",
        boot_info.frame_allocator.managed_frames(),
        boot_info.frame_allocator.free_frames()
    );
    for region in boot_info.memory_map.regions() {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "  [{:#018x}, {:#018x}) {:?}",
            region.start(),
            region.end(),
            region.kind()
        );
    }
    crate::kprintln!("console: COM1 serial (polling)");

    let cpu = &boot_info.cpu_info;
    let vendor = core::str::from_utf8(&cpu.vendor).unwrap_or("unknown");
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU: {} (basic leaf {}, extended leaf {:#x})",
        vendor,
        cpu.max_basic_leaf,
        cpu.max_extended_leaf
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU feature support: SSE2={}, NX={}, 1GiB-pages={}, long-mode={}, LA57-supported={}",
        cpu.has_sse2,
        cpu.has_nx,
        cpu.has_1g_pages,
        cpu.has_long_mode,
        cpu.has_la57
    );
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CPU address widths (bits): physical={:?}, max-linear={:?}, active-linear={} (LA57 active={})",
        cpu.physical_address_bits,
        cpu.max_linear_address_bits,
        cpu.active_linear_address_bits,
        cpu.active_linear_address_bits == 57
    );
}

fn is_valid_pointer<T>(pointer: *const T, virtual_address_bits: u8) -> bool {
    let start = pointer as usize;
    let Some(end) = start.checked_add(size_of::<T>()) else {
        return false;
    };
    !pointer.is_null()
        && start & (align_of::<T>() - 1) == 0
        && is_canonical_virtual_address(start as u64, virtual_address_bits)
        && is_canonical_virtual_address((end - 1) as u64, virtual_address_bits)
}

# Memory-management direction

## What exists now

`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation and classification. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.

`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and coalesces adjacent free ranges. The ownership contract assumes one allocator instance per physical map: within that instance, each eligible frame is owned either by its free-range table or by a non-copyable `Frame` token while allocated. The public constructor does not enforce unique instances, so callers must not initialize multiple allocators for the same physical map; the current boot path retains one allocator in `BootInfo`. `allocate` returns `None` when no free frame remains. `deallocate` consumes the token only on success; on any error, including free-range-table exhaustion, it returns a `DeallocationError` containing the original token and leaves allocator state unchanged. The range tables each have a fixed `MAX_FRAME_RANGES` capacity, so fragmentation can prevent a frame from being returned until nearby ranges coalesce. No kernel service currently allocates frames for mappings or other work.

`Frame::address()` is a physical address value, not a dereferenceable pointer and not a proof that the frame is mapped. CPU diagnostics now read `CR4.LA57` to report the active linear-address width (48 or 57 bits) and query `CPUID.80000008H` for physical and maximum linear-address widths when available. Boot-protocol pointers are checked against the active width, with host tests for 48- and 57-bit canonical boundaries. These facts do not prove that any physical address is mapped.

The requested Limine base revision is 3. Its protocol maps only `Usable`, `BootloaderReclaimable`, `ExecutableAndModules`, and `Framebuffer` memory-map regions into the HHDM; reserved, ACPI, bad, and unknown regions are not in that mapping set. HHDM mappings use at least 4 KiB granularity and may cover page-aligned bytes beyond unaligned region boundaries. On x86_64, inherited HHDM mappings are supervisor RWX, normally write-back cached, with framebuffer mappings write-combining when PAT is available. Therefore an HHDM offset is not a blanket physical-memory access grant, and inherited HHDM permissions are not Rustix's future W^X policy. See the [Limine base revision 3 protocol](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine-protocol/blob/trunk/PROTOCOL.md#base-revision-3) and its memory-layout/caching sections.

The boot snapshot now rejects physical map ranges beyond the reported CPUID physical-address width when that CPUID leaf is available. For base revision 3 HHDM-mapped types, it also validates the page-rounded physical span, checked `offset + address` arithmetic, and canonical endpoints in the active linear-address width. If the CPU does not report a physical width, the physical-bound check is skipped and no mapping caller may treat the bound as known. These checks are derived from metadata and Limine's protocol contract; they do not inspect page tables or prove that a non-null loader pointer is readable. Rustix still does not dereference physical memory through the HHDM. Rustix-owned mappings should be non-executable by default; executable kernel text must be explicit. MMIO requires an explicit device range and cache policy, and guard regions must remain unmapped. A page-table transition must preserve the kernel image, active stacks, boot data, descriptor tables, and any loader mappings still needed. Rustix does not reclaim bootloader memory, own or replace the inherited Limine page tables, or provide a heap. Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup and fatal exception diagnostics live in `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs`; they do not enable maskable IRQs.

## Planned memory layers

1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
2. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; add real allocation callers only after the page-mapping policy and ownership rules are implemented.
3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix still runs on inherited Limine page tables. Before replacing them, preserve the executing kernel, bootstrap/Ring-0 stacks, request/response data, and exception stacks; define the HHDM extent and explicit mapping permissions/cache attributes. Keep writable-executable mappings disallowed by default and reserve MMIO and guard regions.
4. **Heap:** add a global allocator only after frame allocation and page mapping are initialized. Define allocation failure behavior for kernel and interrupt contexts.
5. **Process address spaces:** isolate userspace; define copy-in/copy-out helpers and never treat user pointers as kernel references.

## Invariants to preserve

- Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
- Only complete frames in validated `Usable` regions enter the allocator; the first MiB remains reserved. Firmware and loader-reclaimable regions are not silently promoted to free memory.
- Under the single-allocator-per-physical-map contract, a frame is represented by one allocator-free range or one caller-owned, non-copyable `Frame` token. Only a successful `deallocate` transfers the token back to the allocator; errors return the token and leave allocator ranges and accounting unchanged. The current public constructor relies on callers to enforce unique allocator instances.
- `allocate` returns `None` on frame exhaustion. Metadata-capacity exhaustion is an explicit error, never silent loss of a frame.
- A `Frame` address is physical, not directly dereferenceable. No HHDM translation, page-table mutation, or CR3 switch is permitted until address widths, mapping coverage, permissions/cache attributes, and transition-preservation requirements are established.
- Mapping changes validate alignment, canonical addresses, ownership, and permissions before touching tables.
- User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, exhaustion, and unchanged state/ownership on failure.

These are design requirements for future milestones, not functionality delivered by the current boot summary.

# Boot protocol and kernel entry

## Current boot contract

Rustix currently expects a Limine-compatible x86_64 handoff. Limine is an external loader; it does not implement Rustix's kernel services. The kernel requests protocol base revision 3, the higher-half direct-map (HHDM) offset, and the memory map.

Requests are kept in `.limine_requests_start`, `.limine_requests`, and `.limine_requests_end` by `linker.ld`. The response-bearing request records are mutable and the output `.limine_requests` section is placed in a writable load segment because Limine fills their response pointers before entering Rustix. The ELF entry symbol is `_start`.

### Entry sequence

1. Limine loads the ELF and transfers control to `_start` under the x86_64 Limine protocol.
2. `_start` configures the legacy COM1 UART for polling output and input.
3. The kernel disables maskable interrupts and installs its bootstrap GDT, TSS, and fatal-exception IDT. This does not initialize IRQ delivery.
4. The kernel reads CPU address widths, copies the HHDM and memory-map responses into an owned `BootInfo` snapshot, validates pointers against the active linear width, and validates physical bounds plus page-rounded HHDM arithmetic for the protocol-mapped memory types. It then builds a frame allocator only from validated usable ranges and rejects malformed metadata before starting the shell.
5. The kernel reports validated ranges, frame counts, baseline CPUID features, and address-width facts, then seeds a volatile RAM filesystem and enters Crabshell on the serial console.
6. The shell busy-polls COM1 because no scheduler or UART interrupt handler exists yet. The kernel does not return to the loader.

The memory-map snapshot stores physical regions as checked half-open ranges `[start, end)` and retains Limine's known classifications plus unknown type values. It does not authorize Rustix to access every region, reclaim loader memory, or mutate the current page tables. Rustix checks physical bounds and calculates canonical HHDM ranges for memory types covered by the requested base revision, but does not dereference physical memory through the HHDM or verify the inherited page tables. These metadata checks cannot prove that a Limine-provided non-null pointer is readable; that remains an explicit handoff trust boundary.

## Link and target configuration

- Rust target: `x86_64-unknown-none`
- Linker script: `linker.ld`
- Kernel virtual base: `0xffffffff80000000`
- Required code-generation constraints: kernel code model, static relocation, and disabled red zone
- Rust panic strategy: abort; the panic handler logs and halts

See [`../development/building.md`](../development/building.md) for commands and toolchain setup.

## Failure behavior and limitations

Missing responses, bad pointers/alignment, invalid HHDM values, excessive counts, null entries, address arithmetic overflow, and invalid or overlapping physical ranges reject the complete boot snapshot. `_start` halts before starting Crabshell rather than continuing with partial memory metadata. Structural checks cannot establish that a non-null loader pointer is mapped and readable; that remains an explicit trust assumption of the Limine handoff. The installed exception handlers print fatal context and halt; no fault recovery or maskable IRQ delivery is provided. COM1 writes use a bounded polling loop so a non-responsive UART does not block forever.

The repository includes a Limine v12.9.3 binary archive pin with SHA-256 verification, a hybrid ISO recipe, and a bounded QEMU serial smoke test that checks Crabshell's prompt. On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 on both the working tree and a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory; the clean run fetched and built the pinned Limine host utility, created the image, and QEMU reported boot metadata before reaching the prompt. Milestone 0's local exit criteria are met. Hosted CI has not been observed. There is still no framebuffer console, reboot/shutdown interface, or broader boot-protocol compatibility test. The available serial and keyboard drivers do not imply a general device model.

## Future boot work

The kernel now snapshots and validates the Limine map and preserves firmware and loader-reclaimable classifications without reclaiming them. No region is considered Rustix-owned or free for allocation yet. Loader-reclaimable memory must remain unavailable until Rustix has copied any needed boot data and explicitly reaches a documented reclaim point; ACPI reclaimable memory needs the ACPI tables to be copied or parsed first. Frame allocation, page-table replacement, and ownership transfer remain future work.
